key_insight: A physics-informed neural network jointly updates turbine-blade geometry and flow to match prescribed surface-pressure targets.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a route from experimentally derived blade-loading targets to aerodynamic shape modifications.
method: Constrain the flow with the 2D steady compressible Euler equations.
Use pressure-target continuation and differentiable blade surfaces to update geometry.
Alternate geometry optimisation with flow re-adaptation to moving boundaries.
evidence_signal: On the LS89 cascade with 28 experimental-derived pressure targets, final pressure-side and suction-side RMSEs were 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure; independent SharC verification reproduced the main pressure trends.
watch_item: The evaluation uses a 2D inviscid formulation and a warm-started flow network, with remaining pressure discrepancies near the trailing edge.
paper_title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
